newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate ends at 10/15 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate ends at 10/15 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate ended at 10/15 percent on Friday after trading over a wide range, dealers said.
It traded as high as 45 percent. The overnight closed at 50 percent on Thursday.
Earlier, one-month money was at 15.0/20.0 percent against 9.0/10.0 percent on Thursday.
Three-month money was at 10.0/12.0 percent against 8.5/9.0 percent.
"It will take a while for rates to stabilise," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.

The rise in interbank rates was triggered by a sudden tightening of liquidity in the system as a result of Bank Negara's massive intervention in the foreign exchange market earlier this week to help the ringgit.
Dealers said there was more outflow of funds on Friday from settlement of central bank intervention.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers estimated it to be between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit.
Bank Negara said on Wednesday that it would allow interest rates to rise as part of a move to curb speculation in the ringgit.
Dealers said if Bank Negara does not lend to the market, rates are likely to stay firm next week.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange closed higher after a volatile session.
At the close, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up nine points to 92.30, or an implied yield of 7.70 percent, after trading as low as 92.10.
The December contract was up 12 to 92.55, or 7.45 percent, after a low of 92.30.
